toegepas.voor: wat oor 'n tafelrand uitsteek ook dat
toegepas.na: wat oor 'n tafelrand uitsteek, ook dat
toegepas.rede_vinder: A comma closing the embedded relative clause stops 'uitsteek ook dat' reading as one run and is allowed by the AWS to mark off a subordinate clause.
toegepas.fout: Without a comma after the embedded relative clause, 'uitsteek ook dat' runs together and a Grade 4 reader stumbles before finding where the subject ends.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Closing the relative clause with a comma before the sentence continues is standard Afrikaans punctuation, eases the first reading and changes nothing in the meaning.

laat_vaar.blok: Hoekom die een trom laer klink as die ander
laat_vaar.voor: dieselfde vel stywer of slapper trek
laat_vaar.na: dieselfde vel stywer of slapper span
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'span' is the usual verb for a drumskin and matches 'gespan' used for the same action in the list block, so the learner meets one word for one thing.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Stywer of slapper trek' is natural, clear Afrikaans; 'span' is an equally good word that reads a little oddly with 'slapper', so this is a lateral move rather than a fix.

vlae.teks: Die sand of klein klippies binne die kokonratels ratel wanneer die danser beweeg.
vlae.rede: The protected entry for 'kokonratels' says the compound is always introduced in full first ('ratels van gedroogde kokonne'), but in this lesson it appears without that introduction; a language agent cannot add it, so the writer should check whether it is needed here.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: speel hulle xilofone wat hulle timbila noem
laat_vaar_vorige.na: speel xilofone wat hulle timbila noem
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The double 'hulle' (possessive, then subject) is clumsy; the possessive adds nothing.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The possessive 'hulle xilofone' carries that these are the Chopi's own instruments, set against the school marimba just before; dropping it loses that and the original reads acceptably.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Praat oor julle eie en mekaar se optredes
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Karakters bou' calques English 'build characters'; Afrikaans creates (skep) a character.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Karakters bou' (building up a character) is accepted drama usage in Afrikaans and may echo the curriculum's wording; 'skep' narrows developing to creating, a lateral move at best.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: wat in die middel van jou rug loop.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: wat langs die middel van jou rug af loop.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'In die middel van jou rug loop' can read as walking; 'langs ... af loop' is the idiom for something running down the back.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The ruggraat definition is protected word for word as a shared definition, and 'loop' for something running along the back is ordinary Afrikaans.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Hoog en laag, hard en sag
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Hoog of laag is die vierde van vier ewe goeie vrae
laat_vaar_vorige.na: "Is dit hoog of laag?" is die vierde van vier ewe goeie vrae
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The sentence calls 'hoog of laag' a question, so writing it as the actual question reads more naturally and clearly for a Grade 4 learner.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Calling 'hoog of laag' one of the sorting questions is acceptable shorthand that follows on naturally from the sentences before it, and the proposal adds quotation marks and a question mark to a lesson that holds no questions, so it is only a different way of saying the same thing and adds clutter.
